title: Why Doesn't the Moon Fall to Earth?

scenes.title: Why doesn't the Moon fall?
scenes.narration: Why doesn't the Moon fall straight down to Earth? It actually is falling, all the time.

scenes.title: Gravity pulls inward
scenes.narration: Earth's gravity pulls the Moon inward, just as it pulls a falling ball toward the ground.

scenes.title: Two motions at once
scenes.narration: The Moon is also moving sideways. That motion is essential to understanding its orbit.

scenes.title: A constantly curving path
scenes.narration: As gravity changes the direction of its motion, the Moon keeps missing Earth.

scenes.title: Imagine throwing a ball
scenes.narration: Imagine throwing a ball faster and faster. At high enough speed, the ground curves away beneath it.

scenes.title: That's an orbit
scenes.narration: An orbit is continuous free fall around another object, rather than a straight fall into it.
